articles.title: Harry Kane says England’s World Cup exit ‘hurt more than any other’
articles.summary: ‘It wasn’t the team that we wanted and said we’d be’ England host Spain in Nations League on Saturday. Harry Kane has described England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as his most painful tournament exit because of how the team lost sight of who they were.
body: The captain is determined to move on as quickly as possible and is chasing a statement performance against Spain at Wembley on Saturday night in the Nations League. But he admits he is yet to get over the Argentina game and knows it is something he and his England teammates must work to process.

“It felt like it wasn’t us as a team,” Kane said, as he reflected on how England lost their way in the 2-1 defeat, barely touching the ball after they went ahead in the 55th minute. “It wasn’t the team that we wanted to be and said we’d be. When you maybe go against your beliefs and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing in a way where … if we lose doing it our way you accept it, take it on the chin and move on. It’s tough and it will still be tough.

“I’m so passionate about England and especially because I’ve been on this journey … been to finals, semi‑finals and been so close. Each one hurts in a different way and this one hurt, for sure, more than any other one. I’d say even more than when I missed the penalty in Qatar [in the 2-1 defeat by France in the 2022 World Cup quarter-finals] because of just the manner that it happened.”

articles.title: Netherlands v Germany: Klopp and Xavi begin revival projects with derby
articles.summary: Klopp, with Germany, and Xavi, with the Netherlands, face each other in Nations League after disappointing World Cup for both countries. Before the latest instalment of a time-honoured international rivalry gearing up for two distinct new beginnings, Jürgen Klopp could not resist sprinkling a…
body: In his public appearances Klopp has been on irrepressible form since taking the role in July. The task of whipping Germany back into shape has visibly and audibly topped up the energy levels that had drained by the time he departed Liverpool. Klopp, his wit sharp and appetite piqued, looks a far cry from the character who, to most trained eyes, was going through the motions upon his unveiling as Red Bull’s head of global soccer early last year.

If Xavi is to take the Netherlands, occasionally exciting but frequently unstable during a World Cup run that shuddered to a halt in the last 32, back to their roots it will require a measure of patience. The pool of players does not allow much else; the recall of Borussia Dortmund’s Joey Veerman, who has not played international football for more than two years, speaks of the need for a technically adept midfield fulcrum but otherwise Xavi has scant scope for surprises. Virgil van Dijk will continue as captain despite considering international retirement during the summer; the head coach’s options may feel more complete when Frenkie de Jong and Donyell Malen have returned from injury.

articles.title: GB's Reid and Thomas reach finals at Europeans
articles.summary: Great Britain's Chantelle Reid and Damar Thomas will fight for gold at the European Boxing Championships after semi-final victories on Wednesday.
body: Reid defeated Serbia's Milena Matovic 3-2 in her light-middleweight semi-final, while Thomas triumphed 5-0 over Azerbaijan's Mahammad Abdullayev in the men's super-heavyweight competition.
Team-mates Callum Makin and Dimeji Shittu are also guaranteed medals in the men's middleweight and light-heavyweight divisions respectively after victories in their quarter-finals.

Reid, the Commonwealth Games silver medallist, was behind after the first round against Matovic, but she was the unanimous winner of the second and did enough in the third to seal victory at Asics Arena Sports Hall in Sofia, Bulgaria.
"It was a really good bout. She's a really good girl and I hope we get to share the ring again one day," said Reid.

articles.title: ‘I want to go’: Lewis Hamilton hopes F1 is able to end season in Middle East
articles.summary: ‘I love going to the Middle East,’ says Ferrari driver. Qatar and Abu Dhabi races could still be cancelled. Lewis Hamilton said he hopes the Formula One season can still end at the two scheduled rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, with the finale still in doubt because of the war in the Middle East.
body: Formula One is pressing ahead with its original plan, although a contingency is understood to be in place to host a final round in Imola if the volatile situation means both meetings have to be cancelled.

Speaking before this weekend’s grand prix in Azerbaijan, which borders Iran, Hamilton said he trusted the sport to make the right decision, given the unease among many in the paddock of racing in the region while the conflict continues.

“I personally want to go. I love going to the Middle East,” he said. “From what I have read, things seem OK out there, but I don’t have all the information and I don’t know what the risk levels are. I trust in Stefano [Domenicali, F1’s chief executive] to make the right decision for the sport. And I do hope we get to go there.”

Whether the races take place or not could affect the world championship. Kimi Antonelli leads his Mercedes teammate George Russell by 81 points with nine meetings remaining. If that number was reduced to eight the Italian could close it out even sooner than might be expected. As things stand a lead of 100 points after Mexico, in five races time, or 75 after Brazill would suffice.

articles.title: ‘I had a headache for days’: Hrgovic reveals brutal toll of Itauma world title fight
articles.summary: ‘I didn’t celebrate. I went home to rest. It was a hard fight’ Hrgovic stopped Briton to win the IBF heavyweight title. Filip Hrgovic, the new IBF world heavyweight champion, has offered a candid insight into the ordeal he endured before beating Moses Itauma in a shock stoppage victory last month…
body: “I felt fucked up,” said the 34-year-old Croat. “I received a lot of shots and I was bruised. I had a bit of a headache for a few days. On the Wednesday after the fight I was back in the gym, working out already, but for a few days I felt really tired and bruised, with some headaches.”

Hrgovic, who aims to unify the heavyweight division, said there was a chance he would face Rico Verhoeven, the Dutch fighter who used to be a world kickboxing champion, on the undercard to the much-delayed bout between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury that is expected to finally take place in Cardiff on 11 December.

But revisiting the aftermath of the brutal Itauma bout which changed his life, Hrgovic said: “I didn’t celebrate. I just went home to rest. It was such a hard fight I didn’t even do my tradition after I win, when I go to McDonald’s. I didn’t have the strength.”

articles.title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner
articles.summary: Martyn Jackson never thought he'd play football again when he had a heart transplant in 2024. Less than two years later, he was a World Cup winner with England.
body: When Martyn Jackson walked off the pitch after Ramsbottom United's 2-1 win over Cheadle Town in October 2024, it never crossed his mind that one day he could be a World Cup winner.
In fact, in the days after that match, his goal was just staying alive.
Just a couple of days after the final whistle, Jackson started to feel unwell during the night.
He went into hospital and was diagnosed with myocarditis, an inflammation of the heart usually caused by an infection. Within weeks, he was placed on the super urgent waiting list for a transplant.

Less than two years later, he was a World Cup winner with England.

articles.title: Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo contemplated retirement after the World Cup but wants to reach 1,000 career goals and help a new-look Portugal thrive before hanging up his boots.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring after the World Cup but says he opted to extend his glittering career as he believes he can help Portugal to further success - and reach a personal milestone of 1,000 career goals.
The 41-year-old confirmed in the summer that the 2026 World Cup would be his last, although his long-term future remained uncertain.
However, he has been included in Jorge Jesus' 25-man squad for Portugal's Nations League campaign, which begins against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday night.
In the lead-up to the contest with Craig Bellamy's side, the Al-Nassr forward also targeted the 21 goals needed to reach that magical 1,000 mark.

articles.title: Harry Kane announces he's "fairly close" to extending Bayern contract
articles.summary: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane is closing in on a contract extension that would keep him at the club beyond the summer of 2027. The 33-year-old told The Independent on Wednesday that talks over an extension – reportedly until at least 2029 – are nearing a conclusion. “We're in good talks.
body: “We're in good talks. We're fairly close. There's still some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement," Kane said.
The England forward joined Bayern from Tottenham in 2023 and sees Bavaria as the ideal place to continue his career at the highest level.

“I feel really comfortable in the team, with the coach, the environment. I want to just be at this level and push this level for as long as possible. Especially, as you're getting a bit older, if you don't have a great season somewhere, or you don't play as well, the drop-off is maybe more than what it would have been when you're younger,” Kane said.
“So it's just about extracting as much as I can, with the boss there, with the players I have in the team, I think they're getting the best out of me. I'm helping them as well.”

articles.title: GB sniff Road Worlds chance with Pogacar absence
articles.summary: British riders stand a strong chance of glory at cycling's Road World Championships this weekend, with young talent beginning to blossom at elite level.
body: Great Britain's impressive rider line-up for cycling's Road World Championships means the team have rarely stood a better chance of glory.
For the men, there is also the helpful factor of Slovenian superstar Tadej Pogacar being absent, after he suffered crash injuries during the Vuelta a Espana in August.
But at the same time a new generation of British cycling talent is rising, and GB riders could take the coveted winner's rainbow jersey in the men's and women's road races in Montreal this weekend.

While Pogacar crashed out of the Vuelta, the race showcased the continued emergence of 21-year-old British rider Matthew Brennan, who won five stages of the three-week endurance test for Visma Lease a Bike - a record for a Grand Tour debutant.

articles.title: The Dave Cottle Championship effect: How Waterdogs GM built a winner
articles.summary: When Dave Cottle was hired as the Philadelphia Waterdogs’ general manager last November, he wanted to accomplish one goal for his longtime friend, Bill Tierney: Win a championship. Nearly a...
body: Nearly a year later, Cottle watched confetti fall around his players and coaches after the Waterdogs defeated the Denver Outlaws 14-4 to win the Premier Lacrosse League championship — the second title in team history and the first of Tierney’s tenure in Philly.
For Cottle, though, the most satisfying part of the moment was not necessarily the celebration.

“I learned something about myself. I kind of like the chase more than I like the culmination,” Cottle said. “I like watching the kids after they accomplish and the coaches after they accomplish like that. And to me, that was so satisfying watching them. But to me, I love the chase of it. The competition, finding the right pieces, putting them together. That part of it was really enjoyable for me.”

Finding those pieces became Cottle’s job when he joined the Waterdogs last offseason. After two seasons in which Tierney served as both head coach and GM, Philadelphia separated those responsibilities.

articles.title: Jonah Coleman Pops Up With An Ankle Injury, Opening The Door For A Fantasy Football Sleeper In Denver
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos' backfield has been absolutely ravaged by injuries over two weeks. With RJ Harvey inactive for Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and JK Dobbins exiting the game with a hamstring injury of his own, impressive rookie Jonah Coleman stepped in and looked good.
body: Welp, we just learned that Coleman is now dealing with a sprained ankle. We do not yet know what that means for Week 3, but it's not the news we wanted to hear. If all the backs miss, it could open the door for Tyler Badie to step into a potential near-every-down role.

We were very high on Coleman through the draft process and throughout training camp. So we were excited to see him get a shot at the starting job this week, with both Dobbins and Harvey potentially missing the game. If Coleman is forced to miss Week 3, it would be extremely disappointing.

This will now likely become a situation we have to monitor throughout the week, which is frustrating considering we still have Dobbins returning looming as well. Hopefully, we learn this is a minor concern, and he'll be good to go this week. Nevertheless, you now have to prepare as if there is a chance that he won't be able to go, after most likely just picking him up off the waiver wire in many cases.

With RJ Harvey inactive for Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and JK Dobbins exiting the game with a hamstring injury of his own, impressive rookie Jonah Coleman stepped in and looked good.

articles.title: Does Littler need to change approach to hostile crowds?
articles.summary: Following Luke Littler's latest run-in with a hostile crowd over the weekend, the Sky Sports Love The Darts Podcast has debated whether it is time for the world champion to change his approach.
body: Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.
Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.

articles.title: Bengals’ WR room takes major hit before Steelers game
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are preparing for a divisional road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers with their offense already facing an unexpected personnel adjustment. After opening the season with two wins, Cincinnati now has to reshuffle its receiving options ahead of a matchup that could push the…
body: The Bengals are coming off a 20-6 victory over the Houston Texans. But their preparations for Sunday’s trip to Pittsburgh now include finding another way to manage their wide receiver depth behind Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

The Bengals will be without Andrei Iosivas for at least the next four games after the wide receiver suffered a torn ligament in his thumb and was placed on injured reserve. ESPN’s Ben Baby reported Wednesday that Iosivas underwent surgery to repair the injury, which he sustained during Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over Houston.
“Bengals WR Andrei Iosivas tore a ligament in his thumb and will be placed on IR. Iosivas will be back at some point this season, Taylor said.”

The injury is not expected to end Iosivas’ season. Head coach Zac Taylor said the receiver will be eligible to return later in the year. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Iosivas is expected to miss four to six weeks.

articles.title: Sedlacek wins first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30
articles.summary: Karel Sedlacek secured his first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30, beating Scott Williams 8-7 despite a late scare as he closed in on victory.
body: It was a thrilling encounter, with Sedlacek outlasting Williams' barrage of high scores, which included nine maximums, but both players struggled to close out the victory, with the Czech missing five match darts.

Sedlacek would ultimately claim victory, becoming the first Czech player to win a PDC tour title. But after mounting an epic comeback, winning two of the final three legs, Williams cut a furious figure after the match, shaking hands with his opponent and the officials before throwing his darts onto the ground.
Sedlacek would go 7-5 up before nerves set in, with the 47-year-old needing to check out on 24 to win, before missing a trio of match darts, allowing Williams to pull back a leg.
The momentum turned to Williams, who hit two 140s in the resulting leg, before he pulled the contest back to 7-7.

articles.title: Sky Sports to show England men's tour of South Africa this winter
articles.summary: Sky Sports and Cricket South Africa have extended their longstanding partnership, with Sky Sports and NOW to exclusively broadcast the England men's three-Test and three-ODI tour of South Africa this winter.
body: England's three-Test series against South Africa will take place across December and January, marking England's first Test tour of South Africa in seven years.
The series follows England's first-ever home Test series whitewash of Pakistan and will be Stephen Fleming's first series in charge as England men's Test head coach.

The Test series will be followed by three ODIs in January, as England prepare for the ICC Men's World Cup 2027, which will take place across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia in October and November next year.

Sky Sports will broadcast live coverage of a packed schedule of international cricket from South Africa, with Australia men's tour getting under way this Thursday with the first of three ODIs in Durban, followed by three Tests.
